label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement
text: The createRecord helper mints a new rkey via TID.next().toString(), calls agent.createRecord(did, collection, rkey, record) when that method exists, and otherwise falls back to agent.applyWrites with a create action followed by agent.getRecord; both paths return a com.atproto.repo.strongRef whose uri is at://<did>/<collection>/<rkey> and whose cid falls back to the empty string when the fetched record has none.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createATProto accepts a CreateATProtoOpts bundle of logger, badgeBlueSigner, plcDirectory and agent, and resolves to an ATProto whose DID and signer are read from the supplied agent; it constructs an IdResolver and returns record helpers bound to that agent's DID.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The updateRecord helper takes an existing rkey, calls agent.putRecord(did, collection, rkey, record) when that method exists, and otherwise falls back to agent.applyWrites with an update action followed by agent.getRecord; it returns the same com.atproto.repo.strongRef shape as createRecord, including the empty-string cid fallback.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createMarketClient takes an XrpcService plus an optional MarketClientOptions defaulting to an empty object and returns a MarketClient instance constructed from those two arguments, so callers never build the class directly.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The flow starts every participant in-process on loopback: the dispatcher and fake PLC on port 0 (their real ports read back through `onListen` resolvers), a bidder PDS agent (`createLocalPDSAgent`) plus a bidder ingress relay and `createMarketBidder` with a local compute provider wrapped by `createComputeProviderHooks`, and a requester PDS via `createRequesterPDS` labelled `requester`; each server's abort/shutdown closure is pushed onto `cleanups`.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After the contract returns, `collectRecords` paginates `listRecords` (limit 100 with cursors) for both the requester and bidder repos across the fixed collections `...market.offering`, `...market.rfp`, `...market.bid`, `...market.accept`, `...market.receipt`, `...market.policy`, `...auth.allowlist.rbacDid`, and `...compute.vm`, tagging each record with source label, DID, collection, uri, cid and value; a failure on one collection is logged as `collect error (...)` and does not abort the run.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The script exposes no CLI flags or environment variables: every knob (hostnames, ports, policy, timeouts, collection list, output paths) is fixed in source, so running it requires no arguments beyond `--allow-all`.

label: SpecRequirement
text: `runComputeContract` is invoked on the requester with the `only-me` policy and `bidWindowSec: 15`, `skipSsh: false`, `keepVm: true`, `vmReadyTimeoutSec: 60`, `execProgram: "hostname"`, an SSH session provider from `createSshSessionProvider(logger)`, the bidder DID in `extraBidderDids`, and `did:plc:centraldefaultbidder000000` in `denyBidderDids`; the returned contract object is serialized into the log.

label: SpecRequirement
text: `createFakePlc` provides an in-memory DID directory: `POST /*` stores the posted operation keyed by the URL-decoded path DID, and `GET /*` returns 404 `DID not found: <did>` when absent, otherwise renders a DID document with the two W3C contexts, the stored `alsoKnownAs`, each `verificationMethods` entry as a `Multikey` whose `publicKeyMultibase` strips a leading `did:key:`, and each `services` entry as an `#<name>` service with its type and endpoint.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The run writes exactly three files derived from the script's own directory (`new URL(".", import.meta.url).pathname`): `full-flow.log` with the timestamped log lines, `atproto-records.json` with the collected records pretty-printed, and a generated `SUMMARY.md` containing the requester/bidder DID table, the pretty-printed contract JSON, dispatcher and PLC addresses, a per-collection record-count table, links to the other two artifacts, the reproduce command, the architecture diagram and the SSH tunnel path, stamped with a generation timestamp.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The module is a directly runnable Deno script (shebang `deno run --allow-all`) that performs the whole flow inside `main()` and exits non-zero via `Deno.exit(1)` after logging `FATAL: <err>` if any uncaught error escapes.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Registered cleanups run in reverse registration order, each wrapped in a `try/catch` so one failure cannot stop the rest, followed by a 200 ms settle delay before the flow logs completion.

label: SpecRequirement
text: `installFetchInterceptor` replaces `globalThis.fetch` so requests to `https://plc.directory/` are rewritten to the supplied local PLC base URL, and requests whose host is `localhost`, ends in `.localhost`, or contains `.localhost:` are rewritten to plain `http://` on the dispatcher port (defaulting the port when the host carries none); it returns a restore function that puts the original fetch back, and that restore is registered as a cleanup.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The generated `SUMMARY.md`, `atproto-records.json` and `full-flow.log` are tracked alongside the script as the recorded evidence of the run described in the summary's Participants, Result and record-count sections.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After beginServe, the bidder writes a single machine-readable JSON line to stdout containing event "bidder_ready" plus the bidder DID, the ingress ref and the serve port, so a test harness spawning the process as a subprocess can detect readiness.

text: The CLI config is a single default-exported object named "bidder" whose options map each flag to a type, description, optional env var and optional default, and that object is the only source of the flag/env/default surface consumed by mod.ts.

label: SpecRequirement
text: --offering-refresh-sec defaults to 300 and is converted to milliseconds for createMarketBidder; a value of 0 (or less) is passed as undefined so the refresh loop is disabled.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Exactly one AT Protocol auth mode is chosen in this order: (1) --atproto-oauth, which requires --atproto-handle and exits 1 with an error log when the handle is missing, using createOAuthAgent plus restore/startFlow/completeFlow with a loopback callback server; (2) --atproto-oauth-qr, which registers a genesis did:plc on the PLC directory, restores a saved QR session if present, and otherwise renders a qr.fedfork.com QR and polls for the transferred session; (3) --atproto-handle plus --atproto-password, which creates a local PDS agent; (4) the default, which creates a local PDS agent and runs the association QR flow. Modes 1 and 2 set isOAuth true and leave pdsHostname undefined; modes 3 and 4 set isLocal true and take pdsHostname from the relay ingress host.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The bidder signing key comes from options.privateKeyHex first; only when that is absent is the hex read and trimmed from the file at options.privateKeyHexPath. Every failure to read or write that file is logged as a warning rather than fatal.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The market bidder gets its own serve instance bound to options.serveAddr (default 0.0.0.0), options.servePort (default 0 for a random port) and, when set, a Unix socket at options.serveUnix; its ingress is created unless --no-ingress-proxy is set.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When relay URLs and a visibility hostname are available, verifyRelayVisibility is run against the offering collection for the bidder DID; a positive result logs the indexing relays and a negative result logs a warning with the hint that requester-side listReposByCollection discovery will not find this bidder. label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement
text: An OAuth session-expired error handler logs the session path, deletes the stale session file if present, and exits the process with code 1 after a short flush delay so a supervisor restarts it and re-authenticates.

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement
text: Policy arguments are parsed with parsePolicyArgs, and when --policy is set the name is resolved against the policy registry with side "bidder"; an unknown or wrong-side policy name, or any parse failure, prints "invalid --policy: <error>" and exits with code 2. label: SpecRequirement

Each provider gets its own ingress (with a freshly generated relay keypair) and serve instance, and each serve is begun before startup continues.

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement

intent: This context exists to fix the shared vocabulary of the market bidder before any transport or runtime is chosen. The ABC layering keeps the interface here, in lib/abc, so that the compute and worker bidder implementations can import the same ActiveContract, ContractEvent and CallbackSet without depending on each other, and so a host can supply its own RFP callbacks, accept callback and event callbacks without the bidder knowing how the market is spoken to. Every type here is data or a callback slot: no behavior, no transport, no environment access, which is what lets the same shapes be reused across bidder runtimes.
label: SpecContext
name: lib-abc-market-bidder

intent: This context marks the reserved hono-market package: a namespace and manifest created so the Hono-facing market layer has a declared home in the monorepo's package layout, kept intentionally empty until that layer is implemented here. It exists to hold the module boundary and versioning metadata for the package rather than to provide behaviour today, which is why the entry file is a no-op export and the config carries no dependencies or tasks.
label: SpecContext
name: hono-market

intent: It exists so an operator can run a bidder as a single process — pick an identity/auth mode, enable compute backends, serve XRPC over TCP/Unix with an optional fedproxy ingress, and stay discoverable on AT Protocol relays — without writing any glue code. The declarative config file keeps every flag, env var and default in one auditable place, and mod.ts is the only place that interprets them.
label: SpecContext
name: hono-bidder

intent: This context exists so the did:plc directory server can be launched as a standalone process from a declarative, layer-respecting Deno entrypoint. It carries the process-level wiring only: how the CLI's configuration surface (flags, environment variables, defaults, and the optional config.json override) becomes a bound TCP listener, which Hono app is mounted at the root path, and how the process terminates on signal. The PLC operation storage and directory semantics themselves belong to the hono-factory-did-plc-directory package it depends on; hono-plc's job is composition and lifecycle.
label: SpecContext
name: hono-plc

intent: This context exists so that the marketplace packages do not each re-implement identity, signing, PLC and record-write plumbing. createATProto centralizes how the repo obtains an agent bound to a DID and signer and how records are created and updated against arbitrary collections, while createMarketClient centralizes construction of the market XRPC client over a service. Downstream packages (bidders, gateways, market settlement, trust graph, requester) depend on these two factories rather than on raw agents or raw XRPC services.
label: SpecContext
name: atproto-market

intent: This context exists so that a capability running inside a guest VM has one shared, provider-agnostic interface for the compute contract: it contributes cloud-init before the RFP is sent, is handed its authorization once a bid wins, loses it when the VM is deleted, and is disposed at the end. The derived GrantVars and the subject-key helper exist to keep the guest's presented token subject byte-identical to the subject the issuer's prove handler assembles from the provider's droplet tags, and to keep the audience baked into cloud-init (the requester's own relay DID) distinct from the subject DID (which under OAuth is the user's PDS DID, not the requester's relay DID).
label: SpecContext
name: lib-abc-guest-capability

intent: This context exists so that market logic can be written and tested once against interfaces, and then bound to whatever transport or credential backend a deployment uses. A market implementation depends on this package instead of on a concrete server, which lets pushes over an XRPC endpoint and self-discovered firehose records share the same handlers, and lets settlement be either an x402 paid flow or a free one behind the same Settlement interface. Everything here is types, small pure helpers, and error classes; the host supplies the resolver, logger, signer, and agent.
label: SpecContext
name: lib-abc-market

intent: This context exists as an end-to-end integration harness: it is the executable proof that requester, bidder, provider, relay/dispatcher, PDS, and PLC pieces from the sibling packages actually compose into a successful compute contract (RFP -> bid -> accept -> receipt -> SSH) without any external infrastructure. The script exists to be run manually (`deno run --allow-all compute-contract-full-flow/run_full_flow.ts` from the polyrepo root) and to leave behind machine-readable evidence (`atproto-records.json`, `full-flow.log`) plus a human-readable `SUMMARY.md`, which is why those tracked outputs sit in the same directory.
label: SpecContext
name: compute-contract-full-flow

intent: This context exists so the gateway can be deployed as a process: it is the composition root that turns declarative configuration (flags, environment variables, JSON config) into a running did:web/DID-keyed XRPC service. Everything downstream — DID document serving, service-auth verification of callers, and the requestComputeVM, requestComputeWorkerEphemeral, requestComputeWorkerPersistent and deleteCompute operations — is supplied by the compute-contract-gateway-xrpc implementation and its Hono factory; this package's job is only to read the configuration surface, build those pieces in the right order, bind a listener, and tear the gateway down cleanly on a signal. GOAL.md and README.md extend that intent with a verifiable contract: the README's Quick Start, Request a VM and Request a Deno Worker shell blocks must run end to end against a locally started instance of this CLI, which is what the test:readme task in deno.json is for.
label: SpecContext
name: hono-compute-contract-gateway

intent: This context exists to fix the contract that separates compute provisioning consumers from the gateway transport that actually talks to a PDS and a VM provider. By naming ComputeContractGateway as a standalone interface in the abc layer, callers in the market can request a VM or an ephemeral or persistent worker and delete an existing compute receipt without importing the xrpc implementation or its dependencies on requester PDS wiring, SSH session providers and cloud-init helpers. The interface also pins the lifecycle obligation that a gateway must be started before use and torn down afterwards, and pins the shared shapes (CallerIdentity, ComputeRequestVMInput, ComputeRequestWorkerInput, GatewayComputeResponse) that cross that boundary, so a second transport or a test double can be substituted without changing call sites.
label: SpecContext
name: lib-abc-compute-contract-gateway
